sections.title: Advanced Ratio Concepts
sections.content: Use proportions and compound ratios. Example: A:B:C = 2:3:5, total ₹1000 → A=₹200, B=₹300, C=₹500.

sections.title: Mixture and Replacement
sections.content: Mix two components in a ratio. Example: Milk:Water = 3:2, total ₹500 → Milk=₹300, Water=₹200.

sections.title: Work and Time Ratio
sections.content: Work done is inversely proportional to time. Example: A alone finishes in 10 days, B alone in 15 → A:B=15:10=3:2.

sections.title: Profit and Loss Ratio
sections.content: Profit share proportional to investment. Example: A invests ₹2000, B ₹3000, total profit ₹500 → A=₹200, B=₹300.

sections.title: Age Problems with Ratios
sections.content: Ratios change over time. Example: Father:Son=5:2, 4 years later=7:3 → find current ages.

sections.title: Compound Ratios
sections.content: Combine two ratios to get a third. Example: A:B=2:3, B:C=4:5 → A:C = 2×4 : 3×5 = 8:15.

sections.title: Partnership with Time
sections.content: Profit = Investment × Time. Example: A ₹2000 for 6 months, B ₹3000 for 4 months → A:B profit=12:12=1:1.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
• Treat unequal time investments as equal.
• Cross-multiply incorrectly.
• Wrong part allocation in mixtures.

sections.title: Quick Tips
sections.content:
• Investment×Time = Profit ratio
• Work×Time = Inverse ratio
• Cross-multiply carefully
